raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Add `safe_get_full_model_grads` for model-wide gradient access after `backward` and before `step`. ZeRO-1/2 uses one coalesced reduction per data-parallel group when supported by the backend, with per-parameter reductions as the fallback. ZeRO-3 uses the existing accessor. AutoTP/AutoEP shards remain local.

The coalesced path shares fragment assembly with `safe_get_full_grad`, including the upstream BF16 fixes: contribute only the owned fragment and prefer FP32 accumulation over the low-precision staging gradient. Parameters owned by another rank still contribute zero buffers to the collective.

Fixes #7644. The open-PR search for #7644 returns this PR.

Synced with upstream `0eb3a8bcc` and resolved the conflicts. `.github` matches upstream exactly; the PR diff contains the utility export, implementation, API documentation, and tensor-fragment tests under `tests/unit/v1/zero`.

Validation on one Apple M4 host, macOS 15.7.3, CPU/Gloo with two worker processes, Python 3.12.12, PyTorch 2.14.1:

- `DS_ACCELERATOR=cpu LOCAL_SIZE=2 DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT=90 python -m pytest tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero_tensor_fragment.py -k 'safe_get_full_model_grads or TestFullModelGrads or full_gradient_reconstruction_uses_only_the_owned_fragment or test_safe_get_full_grad_preserves_fp32_accumulated_average' --torch_ver=2.14.1 -q` — **17 passed**. Covers ZeRO-1/2 FP32 against an ordinary PyTorch model, BF16 with FP32 accumulation on ZeRO-1/2/3, ZeRO-2 CPU optimizer offload and noncontiguous gradients, remote-owned parameters, fallback, and separate groups.
- The two BF16 regression cases failed before the compatibility fix and passed afterward.
- `pre-commit run --files deepspeed/utils/__init__.py deepspeed/utils/tensor_fragment.py docs/code-docs/source/zero3.rst tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero_tensor_fragment.py` — passed.
- `python ci/tests_fetcher.py --base upstream/master` — selects 88 test files, including `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero_tensor_fragment.py`.

GPU, FP16, NVMe-offload, AutoTP/AutoEP, throughput, peak-memory, and convergence measurements remain. This machine has no CUDA accelerator or driver.

Updated with AI assistance. The author has confirmed the DCO statement for `eb0c37c`; maintainer handling of its existing DCO check is pending.

The current implementation handles ZeRO data-parallel groups only. AutoTP and AutoEP use additional tensor/expert-parallel sharding, so this helper does not yet reconstruct their full gradients. I can add dedicated AutoTP/AutoEP coverage and reduction handling if you want this API to support those paths.

> Thanks for the PR, how does this work with when autoTP or autoEP is enabled.

Would it make sense to merge this PR with the scope explicitly limited to ZeRO data-parallel groups, and handle AutoTP/AutoEP support in a follow-up PR?
I can document that limitation clearly in the API and tests. I’m also happy to continue working on the AutoTP/AutoEP extension separately so this PR doesn’t get blocked on the broader parallelism support.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep unmapped ZeRO parameters in the collective**

With ZeRO-1/2, `_init_lp_to_hp_mapping` deliberately leaves `_hp_mapping` as `None` on ranks whose optimizer partition does not overlap a parameter. Skipping those parameters means different ranks build different coalesced buffer lists, so a normal multi-rank model can hang/fail in the collective or return `None` instead of the remotely owned gradient. Managed parameters with a `None` mapping must still enqueue a correctly shaped zero buffer, while only truly unmanaged parameters should be omitted.

@@ -235,6 +240,60 @@ def safe_get_full_grad(param):
     return None
 
 
+def safe_get_full_model_grads(model):
+    """Assemble full gradients for all model parameters with coalesced communication.
+
+    Call on every data-parallel rank with the same model after ``backward`` and
+    before ``step``. ZeRO-1/2 gradients use one coalesced reduction per
+    data-parallel group when the backend supports it. ZeRO-3 uses the existing
+    per-parameter gradient accessor. Each returned gradient covers the parameter
+    on the current tensor/expert-parallel rank; AutoTP/AutoEP shards remain local.
+
+    Args:
+        model (``torch.nn.Module``): A model containing DeepSpeed-managed parameters.
+
+    Returns:
+        Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, None]]: Full gradients keyed by parameter name.
+    """
+    full_grads = {}
+    pending = {}
+    groups = {}
+
+    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
+        if getattr(param, '_hp_grad', None) is None and param.grad is not None:
+            full_grads[name] = param.grad
+            continue
+
+        if hasattr(param, 'ds_id'):
+            full_grads[name] = safe_get_full_grad(param)
+            continue
+
+        if not hasattr(param, '_hp_mapping'):
+            full_grads[name] = None
+            continue
+
+        reduce_buffer = _get_full_hp_grad_buffer(param)
+
+        group = param._dp_group
+        group_id = id(group)
+        if group_id not in pending:
+            pending[group_id] = []
+            groups[group_id] = group
+        pending[group_id].append((name, param, reduce_buffer))
+
+    for group_id, records in pending.items():
+        buffers = [buffer for _, _, buffer in records]
+        if dist.has_all_reduce_coalesced():
+            dist.all_reduce_coalesced(buffers, group=groups[group_id])
+        else:
+            for buffer in buffers:
+                dist.all_reduce(buffer, group=groups[group_id])
+        for name, param, buffer in records:
+            full_grads[name] = buffer.reshape_as(param)
+
+    return full_grads
+

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep unmapped ZeRO parameters in the collective**

With ZeRO-1/2, `_init_lp_to_hp_mapping` deliberately leaves `_hp_mapping` as `None` on ranks whose optimizer partition does not overlap a parameter. Skipping those parameters means different ranks build different coalesced buffer lists, so a normal multi-rank model can hang/fail in the collective or return `None` instead of the remotely owned gradient. Managed parameters with a `None` mapping must still enqueue a correctly shaped zero buffer, while only truly unmanaged parameters should be omitted.

+def safe_get_full_model_grads(model):
+    """Assemble full gradients for all model parameters with coalesced communication.
+
+    Args:
+        model (``torch.nn.Module``): A model containing DeepSpeed-managed parameters.
+
+    Returns:
+        Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, None]]: Full gradients keyed by parameter name.
+    """
+    full_grads = {}
+    pending = {}
+    groups = {}
+
+    for name, param in model.named_parameters():
+        if param.grad is not None:
+            full_grads[name] = param.grad
+            continue
+
+        if hasattr(param, 'ds_id'):
+            # ZeRO-3 uses all-gather per parameter because partitions can have different sizes.
+            full_grads[name] = param._z3_optimizer.get_fp32_grad_for_param(param)
+            continue
+
+        if not hasattr(param, '_hp_mapping') or param._hp_mapping is None:
+            full_grads[name] = None
+            continue
